verifications.claim: The Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) is a 1990 civil rights law.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: The Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) became law in 1990. The ADA is a civil rights law (R1); The Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) is a law that protects people with disabilities from discrimination (R3); Americans with Disabilities Act of 1990 (R4)
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources directly state ADA became law in 1990 and is a civil rights law.

verifications.claim: The ADA prohibits discrimination against individuals with disabilities in all areas of public life, including jobs, schools, transportation, and public/private places.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: prohibits discrimination against individuals with disabilities in all areas of public life, including jobs, schools, transportation, and all public and private places that are open to the general public (R1)
verifications.reasoning: R1 matches the claim verbatim.

verifications.claim: Under ADA Title I, employers with 15 or more employees must provide reasonable accommodations to qualified applicants or employees unless it causes undue hardship.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: Applies to employers with 15 or more employees... provide reasonable accommodations... undue hardship (R3, R9); employers with 15 or more employees... reasonable accommodations... undue hardship (R4, R6)
verifications.reasoning: Sources explicitly state Title I applies to employers with 15+ employees and requires reasonable accommodations unless undue hardship.

verifications.claim: Reasonable accommodations under ADA Title I include modifying equipment.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: acquiring or modifying equipment or devices (R6); provision of adaptive computer equipment... ergonomic work station (R2)
verifications.reasoning: Sources list modifying equipment as an example of reasonable accommodation under Title I.

verifications.claim: Reasonable accommodations under ADA Title I include adjusting schedules.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: part-time or modified work schedules (R6); requests for a more flexible work schedule (R2)
verifications.reasoning: Sources explicitly include schedule adjustments as reasonable accommodations.

verifications.claim: Reasonable accommodations under ADA Title I include making facilities accessible.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: making the workplace readily accessible to and usable by people with disabilities (R6)
verifications.reasoning: R6 directly states making facilities accessible as a reasonable accommodation.

verifications.claim: ADA Title II ensures equal access to services, programs, and activities of state and local government.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: Title II of the ADA protects people with disabilities when they use programs or services run by state and local governments (R3); Prohibits discrimination... by “public entities” such as state and local government agencies. Requires public entities to make their programs, services and activities accessible (R9); Title II (Local and State Government)... excluded from participation in or be denied the benefits of the services, programs, or activities of a public entity (R11)
verifications.reasoning: Sources confirm Title II covers access to state/local government services, programs, activities.

verifications.claim: ADA Title II includes public transportation.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: These programs and services include public transportation (like buses, trains, and subways) (R3); Title II applies to public transportation provided by public entities (R4)
verifications.reasoning: Direct support in sources for Title II covering public transportation.

verifications.claim: ADA Title II includes web/mobile app accessibility.
verifications.label: VAGUE
verifications.evidence: ADA Title II programs and services also include... state and local government websites (R3)
verifications.reasoning: Sources mention websites under Title II, supporting web accessibility, but do not explicitly mention mobile apps.

verifications.claim: ADA Title III requires private entities such as restaurants, hotels, stores, theaters to ensure facilities are accessible.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: Title III... stores, hotels, restaurants... must leave enough room so a person who uses a wheelchair can get around (R3); Public accommodations include... places of lodging... recreation... dining... stores (R4)
verifications.reasoning: Examples match and accessibility requirements are stated.

verifications.claim: ADA Title III requires private entities to make reasonable modifications to policies for people with disabilities.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: Under Title III of the ADA, these places almost always need to make changes to the way they usually do things... They must provide reasonable modifications (R3)
verifications.reasoning: Direct statement on reasonable modifications to policies/practices under Title III.

verifications.claim: The ADA covers individuals with a physical or mental impairment that substantially limits major life activities as having a disability.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: The ADA says you have a disability if your body or brain works differently... physical or mental impairment that substantially limits one or more major life activities (R3); has a physical or mental impairment that substantially limits one or more major life activities (R5); physical or mental impairment that substantially limits a major life activity (R11)
verifications.reasoning: Exact definition matches across sources.

verifications.claim: The ADA covers individuals with a record of such impairment as having a disability.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: The ADA also protects people from discrimination because they: Had a disability in the past (R3); has a history or record of such an impairment (R5)
verifications.reasoning: Sources explicitly include 'record of' or 'history of' impairment.

verifications.claim: The ADA covers individuals perceived as having such an impairment as having a disability.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: Never had a disability, but someone thinks they do (R3); is perceived by others as having such an impairment (R5)
verifications.reasoning: Sources directly state coverage for those 'regarded as' or 'perceived as' having impairment.

verifications.claim: The ADA protects against discrimination in hiring, promotion, and firing.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: treated the same as people without disabilities at work in hiring, firing, training, pay, promotions (R3); job application procedures, hiring, advancement and discharge (R4); hiring, firing, promotion (R6)
verifications.reasoning: Title I explicitly covers these employment areas.

verifications.claim: The ADA ensures equal access to goods and services.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: when buying items and services from businesses open to everyone (R3); purchase goods and services (R5)
verifications.reasoning: Title III ensures access to goods/services in public accommodations.

verifications.claim: The Equal Employment Opportunity Commission (EEOC) enforces ADA Title I.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: Regulated and enforced by the U.S. Equal Employment Opportunity Commission (R3, R9)
verifications.reasoning: Sources confirm EEOC enforces Title I.

verifications.claim: The U.S. Department of Justice enforces ADA Titles II and III.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: Regulated and enforced by the U.S. Department of Justice (R3, R9 for II and III)
verifications.reasoning: Direct confirmation in sources.

verifications.claim: ADA violations can result in lawsuits.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: ADA allows private plaintiffs... numerous cases listed (R4)
verifications.reasoning: Sources detail lawsuits for ADA violations.

verifications.claim: ADA violations can result in court orders to comply.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: injunctive relief (a court order requiring the public accommodation to remedy violations) (R4); order injunctive relief (R8)
verifications.reasoning: Court orders/injunctive relief mentioned as remedy.

verifications.claim: ADA violations can result in significant monetary damages or fines.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: civil penalties... attorneys’ fees... punitive damages up to $300,000 (R4); fined up to $300,000 (R8)
verifications.reasoning: Sources confirm monetary damages and fines for violations.

verifications.claim: Under ADA Title III, penalties can exceed $75,000 for a first violation.
verifications.label: INCORRECT
verifications.evidence: DOJ may also assess civil penalties... not to exceed $50,000 for a first violation (R4)
verifications.reasoning: Sources specify maximum $50,000 for first Title III violation, contradicting claim.

verifications.claim: Under ADA Title III, penalties can exceed $150,000 for subsequent violations.
verifications.label: INCORRECT
verifications.evidence: $100,000 for any subsequent violation (R4)
verifications.reasoning: Sources cap subsequent penalties at $100,000 for Title III, not exceeding $150,000.

verifications.claim: The ADA.gov website emphasizes that Title II and III regulations include requirements for website and mobile application accessibility to ensure equal access to services.
verifications.label: OMITTED
verifications.evidence: No relevant content found
verifications.reasoning: No reference content from ADA.gov or others explicitly states this emphasis on Title II/III regulations for websites/mobile apps.
